Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva

I'm working with the earth sigil to contain my Lust, and the invocation of Fire to embody my Will.

I am beginning to see the Elements and the Gunas in all things.

It encourages me.

I have been reading a book titled KUNDALINI, AGHORA II by Robert E. Svoboda in which a claim by his teacher is made that AGNI (Fire) is the proper element to worship in the Kali Yuga, given that most of the Air, Earth, and Water is corrupted in the environment at this time.

It makes sense to me that the only incorruptible Element could ever be Fire.

I would like to hear how you personally relate to the Elements and the Forces.

I don't know who Robert Svoboda is, or about Kali Yuga but I learned most of what I know about elements, forces, etc, comes from Agrippa .

I've always felt that simply four elements and spirit is too limiting and an incomplete philosophy, but I've not quite been able to pin down what else there would be.

The main problem I have is that the classical elements are processes that can each be broken down further into more simpler substances. They are not things that exist self-evidently the way that most new agers take them. Fire, for instance, is a chemical reaction. It only exists because of air and earth. It is therefore not incorruptible because the nature of the flame depends on its fuel.

Put that into metaphor as you like.

I feel that if I'm going to separate each thing into its forces, I might as well go all the way down to the periodic table. And what good is that going to do me? I'm doing magick, not chemistry. It's better, imo, to balance hot and cool, wet and dry as necessary and forget the elements. It's my understanding is that they're largely illusions anyway, because life's processes are holistic, not discrete.

In the Kali Yuga age everything is topsy turvy and illusion. Everything. Even this. Take for example the teaching that Agni is the proper element to worship; when in fact, this over worship of Agni, I.E. desire, is one of the prime fuels of destructive force at this time.

However, if this works for you, and you feel that this particular practice best suits you, then by all means, invoke away. All is lost in this age anyway. (just be careful of what you think you are, or you will get that when you pass.)

On the other hand, if you wish to seek the highest enlightenment, then this age is the quickest way out of suffering and karmic forces. Of course, it is the hardest and most dangerous too.

Casting off all paradigms, while being as still as one can in all things (as you know, this doesn't literally mean not moving), invoke the name, and listen with all one's might for instructions.

Good Journey.

Chocolate Meringue Pie

Ingredients:

1 9 inch pie crust, baked
Filling:
1 1/4 c. granulated sugar
2 T. all purpose flour
2 T. cornstarch
1/4 t. salt
1 1/2 c. milk
4 egg yolks
2 oz. unsweetened chocolate
1 T. butter
1 t. vanilla
Meringue:
4 egg whites
6 T. sugar
1/4 t. cream of tarter
1/2 t. vanilla

Directions:

  1. In medium saucepan combine sugar, corn starch, flour, and salt.
  2. In a medium bowl beat milk and egg yolks until smooth. Gradually stir this into the sugar mixture, then continue to stir constantly over medium heat until mixture thickens and begins to boil. Stir for one additional minute.
  3. Remove from head and stir in chocolate butter and vanilla until melted.
  4. Pour into baked pie shell and set aside.
  5. Beat 4 egg whites with an electric mixer until soft peaks form.
  6. Continue to beat while slowly adding sugar, cream of tarter, then vanilla until stiff glossy peaks form and all sugar is dissolved.
  7. Spread meringue over warm filling, sealing to the edge of the pastry.
  8. Bake at 350 F for 10-12 minutes or until meringue is golden.
  9. Let cool prior to serving.
